dates.notes: Adopted at the Leaders' Session of the AI Seoul Summit on 21 May 2024.

gaps: Participation is limited to 10 States and the EU; it is not a universal instrument.
The separate Seoul Ministerial Statement of 22 May 2024 (27 States and the EU) is not catalogued or mapped.
The declaration is a leaders' text; it creates no treaty signature or ratification.

issuer.name: Participants in the AI Seoul Summit (Republic of Korea and United Kingdom hosts)

reservations: None: the declaration is not a treaty and has no reservations.
parties.summary: 10 States and the European Union are recorded as participants in the Leaders' Session: Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States, plus the EU. The separate Seoul Ministerial Statement of 22 May 2024 had 27 States and the EU and is not this instrument.
unknowns: No depositary or formal endorsement procedure is published; the GOV.UK text is the source for the participant list.

The relationship between the Leaders' Declaration and the Seoul Ministerial Statement is one of sequence and shared summit context, not of legal succession; no formal link is stated in the texts consulted.

related.note: Company commitments launched at the same summit.

ai_provisions: Whole declaration — safe, innovative and inclusive AI; international cooperation; follow-up to Bletchley
relevance.excluded_scope: Non-binding; no legal obligations or enforcement.
relevance.reason: Leaders' declaration from the AI Seoul Summit, continuing the Bletchley process with commitments to safe, innovative and inclusive AI and international cooperation. It is a political declaration, not a treaty.
